slowest_experiments.experiment: Task-scoped GPU lease and phase journal
Independent admission of all mandated GGUF families

summary: The milestone completed 3 compute-bound experiments in 0.3 minutes. Task-scoped GPU lease and phase journal was the slowest entry at 0.33 minutes, but the supplied data does not explain its phase-level cost. The locked classification does not identify GPU idle on compute-bound work, and no data establishes a parallel multi-model launch.
bottlenecks_identified: Disk modification-time reconstruction and zero-duration entries prevent reliable phase-level comparison.
The records do not join accelerator samples to compute-task phases, model concurrency, or runner selection.
No causal data explains why Task-scoped GPU lease and phase journal was the longest entry.
improvements_suggested: Record monotonic start, end, and phase timestamps for every experiment instead of relying on disk modification times.
Attach task-scoped accelerator samples, declared model concurrency, and runner selection to each compute receipt.
Select DualGPURunner only when a compute task declares multiple models for parallel loading.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Make task-scoped monotonic phase timing the primary timing source.
Correlate accelerator telemetry with each compute-task phase.
Add a concurrency-aware runner selector that uses DualGPURunner only for parallel multi-model work.
meta_reflection: The bounded records identify the execution tail but do not explain it. The task-level GPU-idle classification is false, while missing phase and concurrency context prevents a stronger utilization or runner-efficiency conclusion.
